topic.title: Античит CS2 после ребрендинга: куда пропал VAC Live

evidence.heading: Core terminology and confirmed CS2 timeline
evidence.excerpt: VAC is the broader system; VacNet is the behavioral-analysis lineage; VAC Live describes the in-match verdict experience. The May 2026 change supports a visible rename and notification update, not a newly confirmed model or infrastructure.

evidence.heading: Valve Anti-Cheat (VAC)
evidence.excerpt: Steam Support defines VAC as an automated system for detecting identifiable cheats installed on users' computers and says erroneous VAC bans are removed automatically.

evidence.heading: GDC 2018 VacNet talk
evidence.excerpt: Valve presented deep learning for identifying cheating behavior from game data without additional client-side instrumentation and described regular retraining.

evidence.heading: CS2 release notes, 6 June 2023
evidence.excerpt: VAC can live-ban during a match and terminate the match at the end of the round; the notes also describe Skill Group and XP handling.

evidence.heading: VacNet 3.0 limited test, 19 August 2024
evidence.excerpt: Valve announced initial testing on a limited set of matches and requested reports for incorrectly cancelled matches.

evidence.heading: Official CS2 patch notes, 7 May 2026
evidence.excerpt: The published notes list Cache, music-kit, workshop, and miscellaneous changes but do not document an anti-cheat change.

evidence.heading: Client rename reporting, 8 May 2026
evidence.excerpt: DRAFT5 reports a datamined client-string change from VAC Live to VACNET and a match-chat message identifying the sanctioned player.

evidence.heading: Historical VacNet compute figures
evidence.excerpt: The 2018 CS:GO-era report gives roughly 600,000 5v5 matches per day, four CPU-minutes per match, about 1,700 CPUs, and an expansion to 64 54-core blades. These are historical, not 2026 figures.

strict_rules: Use only supported facts or mark uncertainty explicitly.
Do not present the May 2026 UI/name change as proof of a new model.
Do not present 2018 compute figures as current capacity.
Do not provide operational anti-cheat evasion or cheat-implementation instructions.
